key_insight: TraceLab provides a real-world trace of coding-agent behavior, giving serving researchers the missing workload data needed to understand how agentic LLM systems are actually used. This helps move coding-agent serving from guesses and synthetic benchmarks toward evidence-based optimization.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of realistic, publicly available workload traces for coding agents. Without such data, it is difficult to analyze day-to-day usage patterns, compare agents and model families, or design efficient LLM serving systems for agentic workflows.
method: Collect and release a trace of roughly 4,300 coding-agent sessions from real usage.
Characterize workload patterns across multiple agents and model families to support serving-system analysis.
Provide a dataset intended to fill gaps left by existing public traces and benchmarks, which do not capture real-world coding-agent behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, TraceLab offers a practical foundation for building better schedulers, caches, batching strategies, and resource allocation policies for coding-agent serving. It can also improve benchmarking and make system design decisions more aligned with real usage.
visual_elements: Timeline or pipeline showing a coding-agent session from user request to model calls and tool actions
Bar chart comparing session counts, token usage, or request patterns across agents/model families
Heatmap of workload intensity over time to show bursty or repetitive usage
Dataset/traces icon with a callout highlighting ~4,300 real sessions
paper_title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
paper_authors: Kan Zhu, Mathew Jacob, Chenxi Ma, Yi Pan, Stephanie Wang
